__doc: Reviewed whole-word highlight decisions, checked by validate_rewayah_db.py (gate 'cases') on every build and in CI. Each group pins one rule of highlights.py: for every Hafs word location in 'slots', the rewayat in 'tinted' must have the whole-word tint and those in 'plain' must not. Add a group when a review settles a reading; never edit one to make a build pass.

groups.rule: A question read as a statement or the reverse: two hamzas + long a (ءَاٰ۬مَنتُم) vs Hafs hamza + long a (ءَامَنتُم).
Two hamzas + long a in Hafs and in the rewayah (ءَأَٰلِهَتُنَا, a question in all): no difference.
A hamzat qat' read as a wasl alef (Nafi', Ibn Kathir أَنِ ٱسْرِ), word-initial or after a prefix.
The same farsh after the prefix fa (فَٱسْرِ).
A question read as a statement (Abu 'Amr ٱتَّخَذْنَٰهُمْ).
The second of two hamzas across words, softened or changed at the start of a word: no difference.
The second of two hamzas across words after ٱلْمَلَؤُا۟: no difference.
Warsh naql of a word-initial hamza onto the previous word (also with the tashil of a second hamza, 41:9): no difference.
A hamza vowel of its own after naql (Nafi' إِن for أَن): a difference.
A long a after the hamza (Hafs لَـَٔاتَوْهَا) vs a short one (Nafi', Ibn Kathir لَأَتَوْهَا).
A sukun outside the doubled lam of the article (Abu 'Amr, Ibn Kathir خَلْقَهُۥ).
Qalun's text as the official source writes it (قَال۟; listed as a suspected upstream issue in SOURCES.md).
Tashil of the second hamza in أَءِلَٰهٌ (Warsh also with naql, 27:61): no difference.
ٱلْـَٰٔنَ: Warsh's naql, Qalun's hamza written before the lam of lam-alif: no difference.
ٱلَّٰٓـِٔي: Hafs al-la'i with a ya; the rewayat read al-la'i without it or al-lay: a difference.
آلآن in Yunus: Qalun's naql (Warsh reads the same and takes his sibling's tint).
A vowelless hamza before a dotted waw (ٱلْمَأْوٜىٰ, taqlil only): no difference.
Idkhal (an alef between two hamzas) is never tinted.
Two hamzas (a question) in Hafs; a statement in Ibn Kathir (إِنَّكَ).
Nafi' أَؤُشْهِدُوا۟ (a question, passive) vs Hafs أَشَهِدُوا۟.
A statement in Hafs (إِنَّكُمْ), a question in Ibn Kathir, Abu 'Amr and Shu'bah.
A statement in Hafs (إِنَّ / إِنَّكُمْ), a question in Abu 'Amr and Shu'bah.
Nafi' tashil / ibdal in أَرَءَيْتَ (word-specific, outside Warsh's general hamza rules).
Nafi' hamza in ٱلْأَنۢبِئَآءَ (Warsh also with naql).
Nafi' مُوصَدَةٌ without hamza (Warsh takes Qalun's tint for the same reading).
لِيَهَبَ (Warsh, Abu 'Amr) vs Hafs لِأَهَبَ.
Warsh's ibdal marked with the dot (لِيَ۬لَّا, يُوَ۬اخِذُكُمُ): no difference.
The hamza's seat, a silent alef, the KFGQPC Qalun rasm ya: encoding only.
Qalun 'ٱلسَّيِّئِے': the final ya is not read (encoding only).

al-Bazzi's doubled ta' in wasl (tashdid al-ta'at), at the start of the word or after a prefix: a doubling difference after an alef (وَلَآ تَّيَمَّمُوا۟), a sukun (هَلْ تَّرَبَّصُونَ, إِذْ تَّلَقَّوْنَهُۥ), a nun or tanween before ta (فَإِن تَّوَلَّوْا۟, نَارࣰا تَّلَظَّىٰ) or a vowel (تَكَادُ تَّمَيَّزُ); Qunbul does not double.
al-Bazzi's doubled ta' in words that also differ otherwise (تَّلَقَّفُ for Hafs تَلْقَفُ, تَّنَزَّلُ for Hafs نُنَزِّلُ): the other 4 of his 31 ta's.

A doubled first letter where the previous word merges into it (idgham: a nun or tanween before ي ر م ل و ن, an assimilated letter written without vowel or sukun, al-Susi's idgham kabir, a waw / ya into itself): no difference.
The same idgham in the close rewayat: قُل رَّبِّي, مَن رَّاقࣲ (Hafs's sakt is on the previous word).

Nafi' reads the final alef of ٱلظُّنُونَا, ٱلرَّسُولَا, ٱلسَّبِيلَا in wasl too (Hafs in waqf only, U+06E0; the Nafi' texts never write U+06E0), as Shu'bah; Abu 'Amr never reads it; Ibn Kathir reads like Hafs.
Nafi' reads the alef of لَّٰكِنَّا like Hafs (in waqf only): no difference.
Decision to confirm: Nafi' أَنَا before a hamza with fatha or damma (the alef read in wasl too) is not tinted; Qalun's text does not mark it.
Decision to confirm: Hafs 52:37 ٱلْمُصَۣيْطِرُونَ is read with sad (the small low seen: seen also allowed); the sad readers read like Hafs, Qunbul's seen (U+06DC) differs.

The first of two hamzas across words changed into the waw before it and merged (Qalun, al-Bazzi بِالسُّوِّ إِلَّا), dropped (Abu 'Amr) or kept (Warsh, Qunbul, Shu'bah): the two-hamza rules are not tinted.
Abu 'Amr's case ending (نُكَذِّبُ, وَٱلنُّجُومَ) that al-Susi merges into the next word by idgham kabir: al-Susi takes al-Duri's tint.
Spelling only, the same reading (NAFI_SPELLINGS): بِأَييَّٰمِ (14:5), بِأَيَي۟دࣲ (51:47), وَجَنَا (55:54).
A final long a not read before a wasl alef: Warsh writes 20:135 اِٜه۟تَدَى without its dagger alef, joined to 21:1 (no difference).

Warsh's text as the official source writes it (جَدَلاَ without the iqlab meem, in both official Warsh JSONs and the Word file; listed as a suspected upstream issue in SOURCES.md); Qalun's جَدَلاَۢ is encoding only.

al-Duri's text as the official source writes it (لَقَدۡ جِّئۡنَٰكُم: a sukun on the dal before the doubled jim, in both official al-Duri JSONs and the Word file; listed as a suspected upstream issue in SOURCES.md); al-Susi's لَقَد جِّينَٰكُم is the idgham.
Decision to confirm: Hafs's sakt on مَالِيَهْۜ (69:28); the far rewayat's texts write the idgham into هَّلَكَ (both are valid for every reader) and are tinted as written.
Decision to confirm: Shu'bah reads both hamzas of ءَأَعْجَمِيࣱّ (41:44), Hafs softens the second: tinted.

Decision to confirm: a ha' al-kinaya with sukun in Hafs read with kasra and silah (Warsh أَر۟جِهِۦ, Ibn Kathir فَأَلْقِهِۦ) gets the silah colour only; Qalun's kasra without silah (أَر۟جِهِ) gets the whole-word tint.
Decision to confirm (as above): Ibn Kathir فَأَلْقِهِۦ gets the silah colour only.
